title: Impact of Rent Control Expansion on Urban Rental Prices

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The appropriate causal method for this research is a Difference-in-Differences (DID) approach. This method is suitable because it allows us to compare the changes in rental prices in districts affected by the rent control expansion (treated) with those in districts that were not affected (untreated) over time. The key assumption of DID is the parallel trends assumption, which posits that in the absence of the treatment, the average change in rental prices would have been the same in both the treatment and control groups.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# Read the dataset
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s38_data.csv")

# Run the Difference-in-Differences regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)

# Get a summary of the model
summary_did <- summary(did_model)

# Print the coefficient for the interaction term (treat_x_post)
did_result <- tidy(did_model) %>% filter(term == "treat_x_post")
print("Difference-in-Differences estimate for rent control expansion impact on log rental prices:")
print(did_result)

# Basic robustness check: Include fixed effects for periods
did_model_fe <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post + factor(period), data = df)
summary_did_fe <- summary(did_model_fe)

# Compare the results with fixed effects included
did_result_fe <- tidy(did_model_fe) %>% filter(term == "treat_x_post")
print("DID estimate with period fixed effects:")
print(did_result_fe)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect the sign of the treatment effect (coefficient on `treat_x_post`) to be negative, suggesting that the expansion of rent control policies reduces rental prices in treated urban districts. Given that rent control generally restricts the ability of landlords to increase rents, the magnitude is expected to be moderately negative. However, the exact magnitude would depend on many factors, including the extent and strictness of the rent control policy implemented.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log rental prices over time between treated and untreated districts.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The expansion of rent control policies led to a decrease in log rental prices in treated districts.
